scope: Verify whole OBJECTS rollback, same-writer retry and typed readback for IMAGEDEF callback rejection and a core IMAGEDEF allocation failure.

behavior: The existing IMAGEDEF failure/retry control covers entity-stage rejection and consumer OBJECTS callback validation/bad_alloc after the core has staged NOD, GROUP, IMAGEDEF dictionary, reactor, and IMAGEDEF records.

A calibrated ASCII/Binary control measures allocations between the end of ENTITIES and the adapter OBJECTS callback, then injects one failure at the final allocation on the successful core OBJECTS path with a generated IMAGEDEF as the only added object family.
The core allocation failure occurs before the adapter callback; the OBJECTS record scope and whole-file transaction preserve the existing destination and clear derived entity identities.
The same writer retries after the one-shot allocation failure; a fresh typed DXF import verifies IMAGE and IMAGEDEF data in both encodings.
The allocation injector disables itself when it fires to avoid cascading failures during error reporting. No repository DWG/DXF fixtures are added and no support claim is established.

normalFocused.coverage: ASCII/Binary callback validation and bad_alloc rollback/retry/readback, plus calibrated core OBJECTS final-allocation failure, destination preservation, derived identity rollback, same-writer retry, and typed IMAGE/IMAGEDEF readback.

coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.result: PASS in ASCII and Binary DXF
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.counts: 7 allocations in the no-image baseline; 18 allocations with the generated IMAGEDEF path; 11 additional allocations attributable to the IMAGEDEF OBJECTS path.
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.injection: Set the failure countdown to 17 so the 18th and final allocation before the consumer OBJECTS callback fails. Exactly one injected failure is observed and the callback is not reached.
coreObjectsAllocationCalibration.diagnostic: The current build reports emit-failure because the bounded reserve path normalizes the injected bad_alloc; the assertion also permits allocation-failure if a platform path propagates it.

limitations: The core injection covers the final allocation on the generated IMAGEDEF OBJECTS path; allocations in independent core OBJECTS builders and other staged families remain open.
DRW::reserve may normalize bad_alloc into a generic emit-failure diagnostic. The test proves failure atomicity and retry, not diagnostic precision for every allocation site.
Generated round-trip evidence does not qualify native consumer semantics, physical producer breadth, or independent interoperability.
next: Inject allocation failures into independent core OBJECTS builders, then extend failure/retry coverage to other staged families and audit source lifetime, platform numeric/string policies, and scoped concurrency.
